typography.usage: Titles and short section openings; source used style PMSignature.
Reading text, supporting labels and detailed explanations; source used style PMSignature.

recognitionRules: Use a clear name header and a short problem-oriented headline.
Keep the method explanation in one focused evidence paragraph.
Use Arial with restrained spacing and ordinary letter conventions.
Separate relevant experience from any claim about a future employer’s needs.

principles: Name the work and the contribution before describing personal qualities.
Use the identity’s sample as a rhythm and vocabulary reference, not as a factual project claim.
voice.sample: A useful starting point is a problem we can name and a method we can inspect.
voice.sampleStatus: Original fictional brand copy authored for this guide, not a quotation or factual claim.
avoid: Avoid unsupported expertise labels and turning prototypes into shipped outcomes.
Avoid invented testimonials, performance claims and quotation attribution.
voice.secondaryExample: I made this part; the team decided what happened next.
voice.cadence: Short opening, concrete follow-through; vary sentence length for explanation.

logoDirection: Use PROBLEM TO PRACTICE as a plain Arial letterhead. No arrow symbol; the connection belongs in the prose.
invariants: Use a clear name header and a short problem-oriented headline.
Keep the method explanation in one focused evidence paragraph.
Use Arial with restrained spacing and ordinary letter conventions.
adaptations: Tailor the problem statement only when supported by the recipient’s context.
Keep examples concise enough for a one-page letter.
Keep the full name with any new symbol until the audience can recognize it independently.

clearSpaceRule: Keep one half of the main wordmark cap height clear around the full silhouette, including its source-derived supporting device.
